extracted.fund_name: Tuttle Capital Heavy Assets Low Obsolescence ETF
extracted.strategy: Passively tracks the Tuttle Capital Heavy Assets Low Obsolescence Index, which selects ~30-50 large-cap U.S. companies with high tangible asset intensity, durable asset-backed cash flows, and lower intangible/asset-light business model exposure, equal-weighted with sector caps.
extracted.notes: Fund has not yet commenced operations at time of filing. Index is proprietary (Tuttle Capital) but draws its universe from the VettaFi US Equity Large-Cap 500 Index. The anti-AI/intangible-asset positioning is a differentiated marketing angle—index explicitly penalizes info tech and communication services sectors. Equal-weight with ~30-50 constituents means meaningful concentration risk despite diversified ICA status. Index calculated by or in conjunction with ICE Data Indices for sector classification. 'HALO Score' multi-factor framework is novel but entirely rules-based/passive. ETF Opportunities Trust is a multi-series trust already housing other Tuttle funds, so this is a new series rather than a new issuer.

extracted.sponsor: EA Series Trust / Ritholtz Wealth Management LLC (Sub-Adviser)
extracted.strategy: Actively managed ETF using a monthly trend-following model developed by Ritholtz Wealth Management that rotates between U.S. equity exposure (large-cap and tech indexes) and defensive positions (T-bills and low-volatility equities) based on price relative to simple moving averages over six-to-ten month periods.
extracted.notes: Fund had not yet commenced operations as of prospectus date. Non-diversified classification allows concentrated positions. Strategy uses Solactive indexes (GBS US 500 at 60%, US Tech 100 at 40%) for risk-on sleeves and a 50/50 T-bill/low-volatility blend for risk-off. Sub-adviser may override false risk-off signals to reduce whipsaw. EA Series Trust is an established ETF trust (CIK 0001592900) so not a new issuer. Ritholtz Wealth Management is the named sub-adviser, notable as a prominent RIA/media brand entering the active ETF space with a systematic trend product.
